content: 1. Avanafil metabolism is influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised when co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors, as these may reduce avanafil clearance, leading to increased systemic exposure and a higher risk of adverse effects. For patients taking moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, the maximum recommended dose of avanafil (Stendra) is 50 mg, not to exceed once every 24 hours. 2. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of avapritinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Cimetidine enhances the effects of azelastine by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Cimetidine increases the levels of bendamustine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism, potentially reducing the conversion of bendamustine to its active metabolites. This may decrease the concentration of active metabolites. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 5. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Hydromorphone, a minor metabolite of hydrocodone, is formed via CYP2D6-mediated O-demethylation and contributes to the analgesic effect. Caution and monitoring are advised. 6. Berotralstat increases the levels or effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended, and dose adjustments of P-gp substrates may be necessary. 7. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 9. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of bosentan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Bosutinib increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by affecting both CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. When co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor and a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, the brexpiprazole dose should be reduced to one-quarter. 12. Cimetidine decreases the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may lead to premature dissolution, altering drug release and absorption in the duodenum. 13. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, especially with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 14. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 15. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by decreasing its metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required, including plasma level monitoring during concomitant use. 16. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 17. Cimetidine decreases the metabolism of carmustine, potentially enhancing myelotoxicity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of carvedilol by affecting both CYP2C9/10 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of cefdinir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 20. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of cefditoren by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of cefpodoxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 22. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 24. Cimetidine increases the levels of chlordiazepoxide by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Cimetidine increases the toxicity of cilostazol by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider reducing the cilostazol dose, as moderate CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase serum levels of its active metabolite, 3,4-dehydrocilostazol. 26. Cimetidine increases the levels of citalopram by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. The maximum recommended dose of citalopram is 20 mg/day for patients taking CYP2C19 inhibitors due to the risk of QT prolongation. 27. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases cimetidine levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 28. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of clomipramine by affecting CYP1A2, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Cimetidine increases the levels of clonazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Cimetidine decreases the effects of clopidogrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised, as clopidogrel efficacy may be reduced. Clopidogrel's antiplatelet activity depends on its active metabolite, which is partially metabolized by CYP3A4. 31. Cimetidine increases the levels of clorazepate by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 32. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of clozapine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 33. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of codeine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism, preventing its conversion to the active metabolite morphine. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 34. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Cimetidine decreases the levels of crizotinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as drugs that elevate gastric pH may reduce crizotinib solubility and bioavailability. 36. Cimetidine decreases the levels of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised, as drugs altering upper GI tract pH may reduce dabrafenib solubility and bioavailability. 37. Danicopan increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Dose reduction of P-gp substrates may be necessary to avoid serious adverse reactions. 38. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of desipramine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of dexmethylphenidate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the extended-release formulation. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 40. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, with attention to potential adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 41. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of diltiazem by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and competing for renal tubular clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider reducing the diltiazem dose by 50%, and ECG monitoring is recommended. 42. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of disopyramide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 44. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of donepezil by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 45. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of doxepin by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 46. Cimetidine increases the levels of doxepin cream by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 47. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of doxorubicin and doxorubicin liposomal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 48. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of duloxetine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of dutasteride by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 50. Elagolix increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Eliglustat increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates and titrate to clinical effect. 52. Cimetidine increases the levels of eluxadoline by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Eluxadoline also increases cimetidine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 53. Encorafenib increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting BCRP. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor for signs of increased exposure and consider dose adjustments. 54. Cimetidine increases the levels of epirubicin by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Cimetidine increases the AUC of epirubicin by 50%, and its use should be discontinued during epirubicin treatment. 55. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 56. Erdafitinib increases cimetidine levels by decreasing renal clearance. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Consider alternatives that are not OCT2 substrates or reduce the dose of OCT2 substrates based on tolerability. 57. Cimetidine decreases the levels of erlotinib. Avoid combination when possible. If concurrent use is necessary, erlotinib should be taken 10 hours after an H2-antagonist and at least 2 hours before the next dose of the H2-antagonist. 58. Eslicarbazepine acetate increases cimetidine levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 59. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 60. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 61. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ethotoin by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 62. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of etoposide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 63. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of etravirine by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 64. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 65. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of ferric maltol by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 66. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 67. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of finerenone by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustment of either finerenone or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors, and adjust finerenone dosage as needed. 68. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of flecainide by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Flecainide dosage should be carefully titrated, and plasma concentration monitoring is recommended when cimetidine is co-administered or discontinued. 69. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended, as increased adverse effects may occur if co-administered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 70. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of fluoxetine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 71. Cimetidine increases the levels of fluvastatin by decreasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 72. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of fluvoxamine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 73. Cimetidine decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are recommended.
